drills.name: A - the canonical colour is stopped
drills.detected_by: pagentos-bluegreen-reconcile.timer, natural 60 s tick at 09:30:50 (14 s after the fault)
drills.action: reconcile: api-green is not running; starting it from its recorded image

drills.name: B - the colour's image is deleted
drills.fault: container removed, image tag untagged (verified unresolvable before proceeding)
drills.detected_by: natural 60 s tick at 09:33:20 (62 s after the fault)
drills.action: compose rebuilt the missing image from the app tree and started the colour
drills.note: the first two attempts at a 'broken colour' were repaired by restart and by rebuild - which is the supervisor working, not the takeover claim. Recorded because a drill that reports recovery from a fault that did not exist proves nothing.

drills.name: C - a broken release: the colour comes up and never becomes healthy
drills.fault: green's image tag repointed at an image built FROM the real one whose entrypoint exits 1; container recreated. Survives both restart and rebuild - a bad build, a bad migration, a missing dependency.
drills.detection: reconcile started immediately by hand to shorten the production outage; the DECISION is entirely the supervisor's. Detection latency itself is measured by drills A and B (14 s and 62 s, natural timer).
drills.patience_budget_spent: 09:35:29 (container unhealthy) -> 09:37:36 (gave up on green) = 127 s, the documented ~120 s wait_for_colour budget
drills.decision: reconcile: api-green will not come up; api-blue (cedb773...) is the only recorded alternative - taking over LOUDLY (not a completed promotion)
drills.product_reported: degraded at 09:37:50.061Z through the edge - 1.4 s after the takeover, without anyone being told

provenance_preserved.trees: app restored from app.prev; the failed candidate kept as app.interrupted, not deleted

defect_found_by_the_drill.summary: The safety net's alarm disabled the recovery: a failure marker (host state, identical on both colours) made every colour report degraded, and the blue/green release's health gate demanded exact `ok` - so the release that would end the incident could not be promoted. Production had to be unblocked by a human deleting a file, which is the owner becoming the operator (PROJECT_CONSTITUTION / CLAUDE.md).
defect_found_by_the_drill.observed: release of 6683e88 exited 75 'api-green never answered healthy' while docker reported the container healthy; the rollback was clean and blue kept serving throughout
defect_found_by_the_drill.second_instance_same_shape: after the takeover restored cedb773's tree, neither tree matched the bundle pinned from 6683e88, so every tick exited 83 and rewrote the marker - a self-sustaining block
fix: services/api/app/health.py: failing_checks() names the required checks that fail; is_degraded() is now exactly 'that list is non-empty', so the owner's status line and the release gate can never drift
services/api/app/main.py: /v1/system/health publishes 'failing_checks' as a flat top-level string (a shell reads it with one sed expression instead of parsing JSON with regexes)

scripts/cloud/release-cloud-core-bluegreen.sh: the pre-switch gate and the post-cutover edge probe accept a candidate that is degraded ONLY by checks the colour already serving also fails (host-shared, unrepairable by a colour switch) and still refuse anything worse - the same reasoning the reconcile's exit 84 already used
regression_tests: scripts/tests/cloud-release-bluegreen.tests.ps1 (+5 assertions: promoted when shared, refused when worse, refused when it fails the shared one AND one of its own, refused when a release too old to publish the field cannot prove it is no worse)

measured_red.app: removing the payload field fails 2 of the 8 new tests; app/main.py restored from a sha256-verified copy (24c92647...)
measured_red.release_pre_switch_gate: `if false &&` on the subset branch -> 2 FAIL (74/2)
measured_red.release_post_switch_edge_probe: `false &&` on both edge branches -> 1 FAIL (75/1), proving the two halves independently
